summary: Explicit, observable and bounded workflow state for genuinely multi-step business operations, always reaching a defined terminal state after success, retry, compensation or failure. Not a workflow platform.
invariants: S-001 every saga has a stable saga_id
S-002 a saga has explicit state; no undefined partial state is silently accepted
S-003 every step has explicit state and unambiguous identity
S-004 repeated delivery of the same step is safe through the IS-005 idempotency boundary
S-005 step errors are not silently lost
S-006 a failed step has a defined recovery path: retry, compensation or terminal failure
S-007 compensation is itself idempotent and uses the existing authorization and data-owner boundaries
S-008 every saga reaches a defined terminal state: COMPLETED, COMPENSATED or FAILED
S-009 tenant context is immutable throughout the saga; IS-001 remains the source of the effective tenant context and IS-002 remains authoritative for tenant lifecycle
S-010 IS-006 creates no second identity, tenant-context, authorization or idempotency mechanism
S-011 saga and step transitions are auditable and observable with the required correlation context
S-012 a saga cannot bypass component or data-owner boundaries or access another component's internals or data directly

notes: RETRYING is represented at step level, not as a separate global saga state.
A terminal saga never holds a step in RUNNING, RETRYING or COMPENSATING; the store refuses to write such a state.
A transition that is not declared above is refused by the store and writes nothing.

fields.saga_id: stable identity of the workflow, generated or supplied at start
fields.correlation_id: carried on every delivery and recorded on every transition
fields.tenant_id: the effective Tenant resolved by IS-001; immutable for the whole workflow
fields.step_id: declared per step, unique inside one definition
fields.state: the explicit saga and step states of state_model
fields.retry_policy: RetryPolicy(max_attempts, delay_seconds); only a failure the step declared retryable is retried
fields.timeout: StepDefinition.timeout_seconds; an attempt returning past it is a failure, never a silent success
fields.compensation: declared with the step, before it executes; a step with nothing to undo declares an explicit no-op
fields.idempotency: delegated to IS-005 under the command identity saga:<saga_id>:step:<step_id>:<phase>

operations.purpose: start a workflow (resolve the tenant context, create the workflow state)
operations.authorization_operation: none (enforced by the business component each step calls)
operations.idempotency: saga_id is unique; a duplicate saga_id is refused

operations.purpose: run a workflow to a terminal state
operations.authorization_operation: none (enforced by the business component each step calls)
operations.idempotency: safe to deliver again: completed steps replay through IS-005

operations.purpose: deliver or re-deliver exactly one step
operations.authorization_operation: none (enforced by the business component the step calls)

operations.purpose: read workflow state and the audit trail
operations.authorization_operation: none (read-only workflow state of this component)

events.note: IS-006 publishes no inter-component events and implements no event bus (explicit non-goal of Issue #18). The workflow audit journal is owned data, not a public event contract.

data_export_cdc.note: Workflow state is internal and transient in this slice. No CDC infrastructure exists, so none is declared as implemented.

actor_service_id.description: Service identity this executor acts with; recorded on every audit event.

max_sagas.description: Bound of the Level 0 in-memory workflow store. A full store refuses a new workflow instead of growing without limit.

datasets.name: saga_records
datasets.note: Workflow state of each saga: immutable context (saga_id, tenant_id, identity_id, platform_id, correlation/trace/request ids), state and terminal failure information.

datasets.name: step_records
datasets.note: Per-step state, attempt counter, failure information and the workflow fact that the command-safety boundary recorded the effect.

datasets.name: workflow_audit
datasets.note: Append-only journal of every workflow transition, refusal, retry, timeout and compensation failure, with the correlation context of ARCHITECTURE.md §26.

notes: This component owns workflow state and nothing else: no identity, no tenant registry, no permission grant, no idempotency table and no copy of business data belonging to another component.
The value a step's business contract returned is handed to the following steps in process and is not persisted; a step result is not owned saga state.
No credential is persisted: a subject credential is presented per delivery, and the store and the audit journal hold identities only (ARCHITECTURE.md §27).

authn.note: Every delivery presents a subject credential that IS-001 verifies. IS-006 performs no authentication of its own and stores no credential.

authz.decision_source_component: IS-003 Authorization Boundary, asked by the component that owns the data
authz.enforcement_point: the business component each step calls
authz.note: IS-006 grants nothing and decides nothing: it contains no authorization mechanism. A step reaches a data owner through that owner's published contract, so the decision of IS-003 and the enforcement of the data owner apply to steps and to compensations exactly as to any other caller. A refusal is a step failure with a defined recovery path and is never retried as if it were transient.

observability.note: Security-sensitive refusals (tenant mismatch, missing permission, identity mismatch, idempotency conflict) and every terminal transition are recorded with the full correlation context. Replays and conflicts reported by the IS-005 boundary are recorded in the same journal.

dependencies.direction: saga -> idempotency_guard (exactly-once delivery of every step effect and compensation)
dependencies.note: IS-006 implements no second idempotency mechanism: the command identity of a step is delivered to IS-005, which decides between executing, replaying and refusing a conflict.

dependencies.direction: saga -> identity (read-only tenant context of one delivery)
dependencies.note: Consumed through the TenantContextPort of saga.ports; the effective Tenant is resolved by IS-001 and is immutable for the whole workflow.

consumed_at_runtime_by_steps.note: Business steps are declared by the workflow and wired by a composition root to the published contract of whichever component owns the data. The path is always Saga -> component contract -> component data owner; IS-006 holds no store handle, session or internal type of any business component.

non_goals: no Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis, Celery, Temporal or other external workflow engine
no distributed transaction coordinator, no distributed locks
no new OIDC/IAM, tenant-context, authorization or idempotency mechanism
no Component Catalog, Composer, Golden Bundles or Release Trains
no universal DAL and no direct cross-component database access
not a generic workflow platform: a saga is required only for genuinely multi-step operations crossing independent business/data-owner boundaries

level_0_allowance.store: bounded in-memory workflow store (default bound 256 sagas)
level_0_allowance.executor: in-process, deterministic; steps of one workflow are delivered by one thread at a time inside the executor
level_0_allowance.recovery: deterministic retry and compensation, proven by behavioral tests
stated_limitations: A timeout is evaluated when an attempt returns: a hung handler cannot be preempted in this slice.
Recovery is in-process; there is no cross-process recovery and none is claimed.
